subject: Follow-up: EdgePay performance SLOs & burst scaling questions
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@edgepay.com>, Samir Khan <samir@edgepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: EdgePay performance SLOs & burst scaling questions

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard on performance and burst expectations, plus proposed next steps so we can scope a validation run:

Key SLOs you mentioned
- Streaming first-token latency target: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 250ms for real-time payment confirmations.
- Tail latency tolerance for larger payloads: p99 < 800ms (non-blocking).
- Sustained throughput: 300–500 requests/sec for peak batch windows (10–15 minute spikes).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~40, occasional bursts to ~250 concurrent streams when merchants batch settlements.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA desired for production.

Autoscaling / burst behavior notes from the call
- You want warm pool instances to cover the first 40–60 concurrent streams to avoid queueing on short spikes.
- For large ramp events (minutes-long), you expect the system to scale to full capacity within ~90s; for short microbursts (<60s) you'd prefer graceful degradation (queued requests or fallback to a cheaper model) rather than long cold-start waits.

Open clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) For streaming use, is startup jitter (first-token variance) more important than absolute p99 tail?
2) Are there specific regions where >50% of traffic will originate (we noted US-East and US-West)?
3) Do you need request-level audit logs retained >90 days for settlements?

Proposed next steps
- We’ll share a short test plan (attached: edgepay-slo-testplan.xlsx) with load profiles and Prometheus-compatible metrics we’ll collect.
- Schedule a 2-hour validation window next week to run a ramp test simulating a 10–12 minute surge (we recommend Tuesday 4/6 AM PST or Wednesday 4/7 PM PST) — please call out preferred windows.
- Rishi will draft a warm-pool sizing suggestion and a fallback policy (model downgrade + queueing threshold) and share before the test.
- If procurement needs pricing/term details ahead of a pilot, cc procurement@edgepay.com and we’ll loop in Legal.

Attachments included: edgepay-slo-testplan.xlsx (load scripts + metric list) and a draft mutual action plan (redwood-ma-plan-v1.pdf).

Thanks — we’ll be ready to run the validation once you confirm preferred time slot and answer the 3 clarifying questions above.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@edgepay.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: EdgePay performance SLOs & burst scaling questions

Thanks Monica — this is helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers inline: 

Answers to clarifying questions
1) Streaming jitter vs p99: streaming jitter is more sensitive for customer UX — if you can keep first-token variance low (p95 tight), we can tolerate occasional p99 spikes on heavy payloads. So prioritize predictable startup for streaming connections.
2) Regions: US-East ~65% of traffic, US-West ~25%, EU ~10% (for the pilot we only need US regions).
3) Audit logs: yes, 180 days would be ideal for settlement reconciliation — we can discuss retention options and cost.

Additional notes on behavior we need to validate
- Warm pool: we want a warm pool large enough to handle the first 50 concurrent streaming sessions instantly. If the warm pool is depleted, we prefer a short queued state (max queueing wait 6s) rather than failing requests.
- Scale-up timeline: for larger ramps (multi-minute), we expect full capacity in <120s. For microbursts (<30s) we will tolerate up to 15s queueing if the warm pool handles the initial headroom.

Schedule: Tuesday 6 Apr, 08:00–10:00 PDT works for us for the validation window. Please confirm.

Also looping our infra lead Samir on the thread — Samir, want to add anything about test endpoints or IP allowlists?

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform, EdgePay
ela@edgepay.com

Thanks Elena — Tuesday 6 Apr 08:00–10:00 PDT is booked on our side. Quick actions before the run: 

Action items (owners)
- Monica: send an IAM-safe load script and the test endpoint (attached in the sheet) + a short runbook for production-like signals to flip during the test.
- Rishi: warm-pool sizing proposal (initial recommendation: 60 prewarmed sessions across US-East + 20 across US-West) and fallback policy (queue threshold 40 concurrent beyond warm pool, soft degrade to half-quality model at 12s wait).
- Lauren: metrics dashboard link (we’ll provide a read-only Grafana link during the run).
- EdgePay: confirm IPs to allowlist and provide sample payload sizes (typical/95th/99th).

Notes on success criteria for the validation run
- Startup: first-token p95 < 250ms across all sessions during the 10–12 minute surge.
- Tail: p99 < 1s for >95% of requests (exception for largest payloads).
- No unbounded queueing: median queue wait < 200ms; 95th < 6s.
- No more than 5% of requests should fall back to the degraded model during the ramp.

I’ve attached the edgepay-slo-testplan.xlsx with the load profiles and the step-by-step triggers we discussed. Rishi, I left a couple of warm-pool sizing assumptions in the notes — please update if you think we should adjust.

If procurement needs pricing tied to the pilot, I can share a short pilot quote that covers the validation window and a follow-on 30-day pilot capacity.

See you on Tuesday — Monica
